title: Welcome to Engineering (wiki home)
body:
Welcome! We're glad you're here. This page is the starting point for your first few weeks.

Day one: your laptop will be waiting at reception or couriered to you. Log in with the credentials IT emailed to your personal address, then follow the MDM enrolment prompt that appears on first login - it walks you through it and takes about ten minutes. If the prompt does not appear, restart and it will.

Your manager will add you to the team Slack channels. Please set a profile photo and put your timezone in your Slack title; we are distributed across four timezones and it matters.

In week one you should complete the mandatory security and data-handling training. You'll get an email from the learning platform with a direct link; it takes about 90 minutes and there is a short quiz at the end. Your manager can see completion status.

Also in week one: book your probation check-in with your manager. Probation is six months, with check-ins at 6 weeks, 3 months and 5 months. Performance reviews run twice a year, in March and September, and are described in the People handbook.

Somewhere in your first fortnight you'll want database access and VPN. Ask in the relevant channel and someone will sort you out.

Ask questions. Nobody expects you to know anything yet.

title: Service Development Guide
body:
This guide covers working on the core service.

Repository: git clone git@github.com:acme/core-service.git. You'll need your SSH key added to your GitHub account and your GitHub account added to the acme org - your manager raises that request in the #it-requests channel using the /access command.

Local setup: we use mise for toolchain management. `mise install` will pick up .mise.toml and install Go 1.23 and Node 22. Then `make bootstrap` creates the local Postgres via docker compose, runs migrations and seeds fixtures. `make test` should pass from a clean checkout - if it does not, the usual cause is a stale docker volume; `make clean-db` fixes it.

Running the frontend against staging: the frontend lives in the same repo under web/. `cd web && npm install && npm run dev:staging` points it at staging.acme.internal. This requires the VPN to be connected, otherwise every request will hang with no error message.

Deploying: merge to main triggers a build. Deploys to staging are automatic on green. Production deploys require an approval in the deploy channel from someone on the service's owner list.

Observability: dashboards are linked from the service README.

title: Platform Runbook: Observability
body:
Our observability stack is Grafana (dashboards), Prometheus (metrics), Loki (logs) and Tempo (traces).

Access: Grafana is behind SSO at grafana.acme.internal. Everyone in the engineering group gets read access automatically on their first SSO login - no request needed. If you get a 403, it means your SSO group sync has not run yet; it runs hourly.

The golden dashboards are: Service Health (per-service RED metrics), Fleet Overview, and Customer Impact. All three are in the 'Golden' folder and are the ones you should look at during an incident.

Alert routing is configured in alertmanager.yaml in the platform repo. Alerts route to the owning team's channel and, for pages, to the on-call.

Incident severity: SEV1 is customer-visible loss of a core flow, SEV2 is degraded core flow or full loss of a non-core flow, SEV3 is everything else that needs coordination. Anyone can declare an incident - you do not need permission and you will never be criticised for declaring one that turns out to be minor. Declare by typing /incident in any channel; that creates the incident channel, pages the incident commander on rota, and starts the timeline.

Being added to the rotation: talk to your team lead when you feel ready. Typically people shadow for two rotations before taking a primary shift.

title: IT Requests: How to ask for things
body:
Most access requests go through the self-service portal at it.acme.internal. Log in with SSO.

Available self-service: additional monitor, docking station, software licences, password reset, MFA device reset.

Not self-service, raise a ticket with the 'Access' category: VPN profiles, database roles, third-party tool seats, elevated cloud permissions. Include your manager in the ticket - approvals are required and tickets without a named approver sit in the queue.

Turnaround is 1-2 business days for standard requests. Urgent requests during an incident: page the IT on-call via the paging app.

A note on the VPN: we use the corporate VPN client which is pushed to your laptop by MDM. It will appear in your applications folder automatically. Connection profiles are issued per-person and are not shareable.

Support tool seats: our support platform is licensed per seat, so read-only access for engineers is granted on request rather than by default. Raise it under 'Access' and specify read-only.

title: People Handbook: Money and Time
body:
Expenses. We use the expenses app, which you'll find in your SSO app list on your first day. Photograph the receipt, pick a category, submit. Claims under 100 are auto-approved. Between 100 and 500 need your manager. Above 500 need your manager and the department head, and anything above 2,000 needs to be pre-approved before you spend it, not after.

Reimbursement runs with the monthly payroll cycle; claims submitted after the 25th land in the following month.

Travel. Book through the travel platform, not directly. Economy for flights under 6 hours.

Leave. Booked in the HR system. There is no fixed allowance for unpaid leave; talk to your manager.

Equipment budget. You have a personal equipment budget for your home setup, renewed every two years. Spend it through the expenses app under 'Home Office'.

Performance reviews are covered in the Growth section of this handbook, not here.

title: Team Norms (the #payments team page)
body:
How we work.

Standup is 09:45 in the team channel, written not spoken. Post what you did, what you're doing, and anything blocking you.

We pair on anything touching money movement. Not optional.

Code review: two approvals for anything in the ledger path, one elsewhere. We aim to review within four working hours.

Channels you should be in: #payments (team), #payments-alerts (noisy, mute it but do not leave it), #eng-general, #incidents, and #deploys. Your manager adds you to the first two; the rest are open, just join them.

On-call: the payments rotation is one week in five. New joiners shadow for two full rotations before going primary. Your first shadow week is usually in your second month, not your second week - we have found earlier does not help anyone.

Docs we maintain: the ledger design doc, the reconciliation runbook, and the PSP integration notes. All in the team folder.

If you are stuck for more than 30 minutes, ask. Seriously.
